about: Parametric motion (docs/apcalcbc-spec.md section 6; builder T2). The paths and every number live in calculus-bc/assets/tools/math/parametric-motion.js; contexts unlock with their Unit 9 topics. Checked by scripts/lib/apcalcbc-tool-checks/parametric-motion.mjs.
intro: A particle traced by $x(t)$ and $y(t)$, with its velocity and acceleration vectors drawn as it moves. Press Play or drag the particle along its path. The readouts give the speed, the slope $\frac{dy}{dx}$ and the concavity; the graph under the path is the speed, and the area under it is the distance traveled. With velocity given (9.5), watch the position build from the starting point.
howItWorks:
• Velocity is the vector $\left\langle x'(t), y'(t) \right\rangle$, drawn from the particle and always tangent to the path. Acceleration is $\left\langle x''(t), y''(t) \right\rangle$.
  • Speed is the length of the velocity vector, $\sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2}$, never $\left|\frac{dy}{dx}\right|$.
  • Slope: $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}$ where $\frac{dx}{dt} \ne 0$. Where $\frac{dx}{dt} = 0$ and $\frac{dy}{dt} \ne 0$ the tangent is vertical; where both are 0 the particle stops.
  • Concavity: $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)}{dx/dt}$, divided by $\frac{dx}{dt}$ once more.
  • Distance traveled is $\int_a^b \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2}\,dt$, the area under the speed graph, computed numerically (adaptive Simpson). With velocity given, $x(t) = x(a) + \int_a^t x'(s)\,ds$, and the same for $y$.
  • The arrows are scaled to each path's largest velocity and acceleration, so compare lengths along one path, not between paths.
